2 REFERENCE PETITION UNDER SECTION 18 OF THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT, 1894 J U D G M E N T / AWARD (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 15 3.

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 2005-06 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded owner/ co-bhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no.10//19(4-16), 22 (4-16), 14//1(4-12), 2(4-16), 18//21(4-16), 22(1-14), 26//4/1 (3-16), 5(4-16),
27//1(4-01), 29//9(4-16), 12 min(4-14) of total land 47 bigha 13 biswas having 1/4th each share situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are the owner/co-bhumidar and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.

The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 6.

sentences.text: The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 15

entities.text: Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 14.09.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.

(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 15 allottees of the residential plots/flats.

therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
( vi )
The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2- 3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

sentences.text: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Mubarakpur Dabas and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH-8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

(ix) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 15 Rs. 5000 per square metre, however, the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
11. It is submitted that the said land, after acquisition the possession of the same has been taken back by the L&B department from DDA and subsequently handed over to RPD VII.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh &
ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 15 petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 2005-06 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 6.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate Ishwar Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Kalan) on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193982472/
3 and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 15
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 15 allottees of the residential plots/flats.
The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.
The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
Counsels for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.
opennyai_summary.decision:
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 20.
has been given.
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 22.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
(1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
LAC no.36916 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ishwar Singh & ors. v. Union of India Page no. 14 of 15 (4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23. Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
